inline_comments.comment:
`role="status"` is hardcoded regardless of the `politeness` prop. Per the ARIA spec, `role="status"` carries an implicit `aria-live="polite"`. Using it alongside `aria-live="assertive"` creates a semantic contradiction: the role signals polite behavior while the explicit attribute demands immediate interruption. The correct role for assertive announcements is `role="alert"`, which itself has an implicit `aria-live="assertive"`. Consider:

```tsx
role={politeness === 'assertive' ? 'alert' : 'status'}
```

Note that the `PolitenessToggle` and `VisibleFormError` story play functions both query by `getByRole('status')` after switching to assertive politeness — they would also need updating if the role is made dynamic.

The JSDoc claims the hook "Cleans up the announcer on unmount", but neither `useEffect` call returns a cleanup function — `destroyAnnouncer()` or `clearAnnouncer(politeness)` is never invoked when the component unmounts. `@react-aria/live-announcer` injects DOM nodes outside the React tree that accumulate if never destroyed. Either add the cleanup:

```tsx
useEffect(() => () => destroyAnnouncer(), []);
```

or remove the misleading claim from the documentation.

`export const announce: typeof ariaAnnounce = ariaAnnounce` is an indirect re-export that reads as a new value binding rather than a pass-through. The aliasing to `ariaAnnounce` is only needed because the name is used inside `useAnnouncer`. `clearAnnouncer` and `destroyAnnouncer` (line 69) are never used internally at all. Both can be simplified to direct re-exports:

```tsx
export { clearAnnouncer, destroyAnnouncer } from '@react-aria/live-announcer';
```

For `announce`, either use a direct re-export too and reference `ariaAnnounce` only where used, or at minimum use the standard re-export form `export { announce } from '@react-aria/live-announcer'`.

The JSDoc says `"string for exact match"` but the implementation on line 59 uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a substring check — `text: 'passed'` would match `'3 tests passed today'`. The comment should read `"substring match"`, or the implementation should use `content === text` (or `content.trim() === text`) for a true exact match. This discrepancy could cause tests to pass when they should fail, masking assertion bugs.

general_comments.comment: `LiveRegion.tsx` bundles two independent announcement mechanisms in one module: the declarative `<LiveRegion>` component (which relies on the browser's native aria-live DOM mutation tracking) and the imperative `announce()` / `useAnnouncer()` API (which uses `@react-aria/live-announcer` to inject separate DOM nodes entirely outside the React tree). A developer unfamiliar with this could reasonably assume `announce()` updates the `<LiveRegion>` component, or use both for the same message and inadvertently produce double announcements. Adding a note to the module-level or component JSDoc explicitly stating that these are two distinct pathways — and offering guidance on when to prefer each — would prevent this confusion.
